metaDescription: La Granja #1 santol is a santol variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: La Granja #1 is a registered santol variety, also sold or known as La Granja santol or NSIC Sn 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2001 as NSIC 2001 Sn 01. Its record notes a yield of 1,200 kg.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for La Granja santol or NSIC Sn 01, this is the same santol. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [santol variety finder](/crop-varieties/santol), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about La Granja #1 santol
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of La Granja #1 was about 12 to 15 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 1,200 kg. It bears every year, with fruit in December February. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit santol fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of La Granja #1 weighs about 400.9 grams, and its shape is ovoid. The flesh is white and soft. Its sweetness measured 18.01 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 42.15 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is December February, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Ovoid, about 400 g, smooth yellow skin, soft, juicy, sweet white pulp, about 18 Brix, about 42 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the Negros santol with big, sweet fruit (about 400 g) and about 1,200 kg per tree. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant La Granja #1 santol

Bangkok santol is big and sweet. Pick a selection by fruit size and a thick, sweet rind. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is La Granja santol the same as La Granja #1?
items.a: Yes. La Granja santol is another name for La Granja #1, registered as NSIC 2001 Sn 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 1,200 kg. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of La Granja #1?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
